description: Write a pandas ETL script for health_portal that validates appointment records against a set of rules and splits them into a valid output and a rejects output with reasons. Rules: (R1) appointment_id is not null and unique within the file (the first occurrence is valid, later ones are rejected), (R2) patient_id matches ^P\d{6}$, (R3) scheduled_at parses as an ISO 8601 timestamp, (R4) duration_min is an integer between 5 and 480 inclusive, (R5) status is one of booked, completed, cancelled, no_show (case-insensitive, stored lower case). A record failing several rules must list all failed rules. The script must print a summary and exit non-zero if more than 20% of records are rejected.
edge_cases: A2 fails two rules and both must be reported
The duplicate A1 keeps the first occurrence as valid and rejects the second
duration_min arrives as a string in some rows; '45' is valid, boundary value 5 is valid
valid + rejects row counts must equal the input row count
In the sample 3 of 5 records are rejected (60%), so the script must exit non-zero after writing both outputs
common_failure_modes: FM7: pd.to_datetime(errors='coerce') turns bad dates into NaT that pass through as valid rows
FM7: drop_duplicates removes the second A1 without recording a reject
FM7: Reject threshold computed but never enforced via exit code
